title: DoorDash said it’s only received ‘several hundred’ orders from AI agents
slides: DoorDash's AI agent orders: several hundred. Why so few?
AI agents can now order food through chat interfaces
But human browsing still drives nearly all the volume
Your delivery experience won't change because of this yet
Test an AI order yourself — see what breaks
thread_text:
1. The 200 Orders That Didn't Happen

DoorDash's AI agent can take orders via chat, but only a few hundred people tried it. Human browsing still drives almost all deliveries.

2. Chat Ordering Exists, Barely Used

You can now order food by messaging an AI, but almost nobody does. The feature is live, yet the volume is negligible.

3. Why Humans Still Click Menus

Browsing lets you discover and compare; chatting feels like a transaction. The habit gap explains the tiny numbers.

4. Your Delivery Won't Change Yet

Restaurants and drivers see no shift because AI orders are a rounding error. The experience stays the same for now.

5. Test the AI Order Yourself

Open DoorDash's AI chat and order lunch. Note what breaks or feels slow—then ask if you'd do it again tomorrow.

A few hundred orders. That's all DoorDash's AI agent has processed since launch. 🍔

You can order food by chatting with an AI now, but almost nobody does it.

Human browsing still drives nearly every delivery on the platform.

The gap: clicking menus lets you discover and compare, chatting feels purely transactional.

For now, nothing changes in your delivery workflow or how restaurants operate. AI orders are a rounding error.

Would you actually order lunch through a chat window tomorrow, or go back to scrolling? 🤔
